rationale: Tests the WHO definition of diarrhoea (duration-based classification: acute <14 days, persistent 14-28 days, chronic >4 weeks) covered in the Classification block.
Tests understanding of secretory vs osmotic diarrhoea — specifically whether secretory diarrhoea persists on fasting, which is a key distinguishing feature covered in the Pathophysiology block.

Tests the application of history-taking approach — specifically what stool characteristics help distinguish invasive from non-invasive pathogens, a key clinical skill covered in the history-taking block.

Tests the principle of differential diagnosis generation — specifically that the pattern of examination findings (fever, hepatomegaly, right iliac fossa tenderness) can help localise the aetiology; covered in the Interpretation block.

Tests the key procedural skill of microscopic identification of intestinal parasites — specifically distinguishing E. histolytica trophozoites (with ingested RBCs) from non-pathogenic amoebae, covered in the parasite microscopy block.
Tests understanding of the hanging-drop preparation technique for Vibrio cholerae — specifically its characteristic darting motility, covered in the Vibrio cholerae microscopy block.

Tests application of the WHO ORS Plan B — specifically the correct volume (75 mL/kg) and duration (4 hours) for moderate dehydration, a critical treatment calculation covered in the Rehydration block.

Tests understanding of the antiparasitic pharmacotherapy principle — specifically that metronidazole is the first-line drug for both giardiasis AND intestinal amoebiasis, covered in the Parasitic Pharmacotherapy block.
